newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Petkoff calls for wage restraint.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Petkoff calls for wage restraint.

text.p: Venezuela's Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff urged public sector employees on Tuesday to show restraint in their wage demands in order to allow the country to reach the goal of 25 percent inflation this year.
"If the government maintains fiscal displine, and this has to do with public sector salaries, we'll have inflation of 25 percent this year, which is quite attainable," he said.
Inflation in Venezuela closed 1996 at a record 103.2 percent. Petkoff said last week the inflation rate in January is expected to be 2.0 percent, down from 3.0 percent in December.
Petkoff, speaking to Union Radio, reiterated that public spending had to be tightly controlled -- "if not, inflation will spin out of control."
His comments were indirectly aimed at public doctors who have been on strike for 12 days over a pay dispute, taking Venezuela's shaky health system to the brink of collapse.
